Despite its historical association with comb-making, Hang Luoc Street today is perhaps best known for its annual flower market, which takes place during the Tet holiday season, typically from the 23rd day of the twelfth lunar month until New Year's Eve. This tradition began when the nearby Dong Xuan Market replaced the old Cau Dong Market, which had been situated along the banks of the To Lich River.

As the flower trade expanded, vendors found that the Dong Xuan Market could not accommodate the growing number of flower sellers, leading them to seek out new locations. By the early 20th century, Hang Luoc Street emerged as a popular spot for flower vendors, especially during the Tet holiday, when the street transforms into a vibrant marketplace filled with an array of flowers such as peach blossoms, apricot blossoms, and various other blooms from nearby areas like Quang Ba and Nhat Tan.
